name: Portable, persistent KV state layer for self-hosters (open-core infrastructure software)
one_line: An Apache-2.0 vLLM/SGLang connector plus state store that makes session KV a durable, tenant-keyed, audited object that survives pod death and resumes on any replica with bit-identical output (proven at TP=1), with a commercial fleet control plane as the paid layer; speed parity vs re-prefill is a gate, not the headline.

founder_decisions.decision: Does the presence of LMCache/Tensormesh, Mooncake, NVIDIA KVBM/NIXL, llm-d and vLLM's in-tree OffloadingConnector on the same KVConnector seam disqualify this direction, or merely define its baselines?
founder_decisions.options: (a) Proceed and treat them as the named baselines in the Week 4 benchmark; (b) build on top of one of them (LMCache L2 adapters, NIXL, Mooncake) as transport and differentiate only on durability/governance/control plane; (c) stop. Evidence that informs it: the parity benchmark result, and whether any of them ship durable pod-death survival, tenant keying and audit logs by then (none documented today per the research files).
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: The founder's hard rule: a competitor's existence is not a disqualifier; the facts are stated neutrally in section 9 and the judgment about adjacency is the founder's.

founder_decisions.decision: Is the governance-first buyer segment (regulated, sovereign, neocloud platform teams) large enough to build for?
founder_decisions.options: Unmeasured; no customer interviews exist in either repo. Options: run five-partner outreach during the 6-week build; commission a survey of self-hosting agent teams (none found in research files); or proceed on conviction. Evidence: partner conversion (kill gate 0 of 5 / proceed 2 of 5).
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Market-size judgments are explicitly reserved for the founder.

founder_decisions.decision: Hosted control plane vs BYOC vs pure open source
founder_decisions.options: (a) Apache-2.0 core only, customer-operated (README's stated scope); (b) BYOC control plane installed in the customer's cluster; (c) hosted multi-tenant control plane (what edge/ and dexa_platform prototype, contradicting the README per 04-conflicts #7). Evidence: which partners will pay, and for which surface.
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: An operating-model and go-to-market choice with no measured evidence either way; the repo itself holds all three framings.

founder_decisions.decision: Own the durable store or use LMCache/NIXL/Mooncake as transport underneath the state layer
founder_decisions.options: (a) Own pinned-slab + NVMe + S3 store (voice connector design, 22 GB/s-class pinned RAM path); (b) reuse LMCache's 21 L2 adapters or NIXL plugins and add only keying, durability semantics and governance; (c) hybrid. Evidence: measured transfer rates (22 GB/s pinned CPU vs ~0.6 GB/s Volume), the connector API drift count, and dependency risk on projects whose roadmaps (LMCache Q2-2026, vLLM TieringManager RFC) may absorb the same features.
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: A build-vs-depend judgment that trades engineering control against upstream absorption risk; both sides have facts, no measurement decides it.

founder_decisions.decision: Engine order: vLLM first, SGLang first, or Dynamo
founder_decisions.options: vLLM (all repo evidence, 0.24.0 conformance, but API 'experimental'); SGLang (HiCacheStorage ABC, session RFCs open, no repo evidence); Dynamo/KVBM (standalone kvbm package, no published perf). Evidence: partner engine mix and the API-drift measurement.
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Depends on the customers the founder chooses; the repo only measured vLLM.

founder_decisions.decision: GPU class and model class to target
founder_decisions.options: Small-HBM fleets (L40S/A10G, where the measured memory wall exists) vs 80 GB+ parts (H100/H200/B200, unmeasured; both repos call this the top threat) and 7-8B TP=1 models (measured) vs large TP>1 models where 'TP=8 keeps eight copies' (unbuilt). Evidence: the H100 re-runs listed in 04-conflicts #5 and the TP>1 experiment.
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Changes the build order and the value story; only the founder can weigh which fleet the company sells into.

founder_decisions.decision: Fork vLLM for scheduler-native prefetch and eviction ordering, or stay out-of-tree
founder_decisions.options: (a) Out-of-tree connector only (what the KVConnector API allows: save-at-prefill, restore-on-match, delay-free); (b) maintain a vLLM patch/fork for request-less prefetch and eviction ordering (the voice repo's 'strongest remaining version' of its thesis, untested); (c) upstream the needed hooks. Evidence: API drift rate and whether out-of-tree passes the kill gates.
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: A maintenance-burden vs capability trade-off the founder must own.

founder_decisions.decision: Is the mutation/versioning/branching DAG the product, or a later substrate?
founder_decisions.options: (a) Lead with durability/governance (measured foundation) and defer the DAG; (b) lead with mutable versioned state (README's original wedge; HF-only, CPU tiny-model tests, 4.6x token-count reduction, no GPU wall time); (c) drop it. Evidence: a GPU wall-time measurement of recompute_incremental inside vLLM at 32k-64k (unrun).
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Product-identity choice; the evidence for the DAG is design-level and the founder decides how much unproven vision to carry.

founder_decisions.options: Per-GPU under management (expressible today); savings-share like Tensormesh's 30%-of-estimated-savings (expressible only after a measured recompute-avoided metric exists); per-token $0-cached (only if the founder also becomes a token provider). Evidence: the Week 5 metric and partner willingness.
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Commercial choice that also dictates which instrumentation is built first.

founder_decisions.decision: Upstream posture: contribute to vLLM's TieringManager RFC #38260 and SGLang's session RFCs, or differentiate out-of-tree
founder_decisions.options: (a) Upstream keying/durability primitives and keep governance/control plane proprietary; (b) stay fully out-of-tree; (c) fully open including control plane. Evidence: whether upstream RFCs ship durable/multi-tenant semantics within the build window.
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Open-core boundary and community-strategy decision; the README's 'never cripple the core' rule is a founder value, not a measurement.
